reconstructed_theorem_text:
For every natural number n at least 3, every real number κ at least 4, and every nonnegative real number ℓ, consider the full real orthogonal group O(n), including both determinant signs, with its normalized Haar probability measure H. For O in this group set U(O)=O₀₀, a(O)=κ+1+4ℓ−(κ−1)U(O), and A(O)=((κ+1)/2)I−((κ−1)/4)(O+Oᵀ). On Euclidean Rⁿ let t(x)=exp(−ℓ‖x‖²), let γ(O) be the existing centered multivariate Gaussian measure with covariance A(O)⁻¹, and set p(O,x)=sqrt(det A(O))/(2π)^(n/2) times exp(−xᵀA(O)x/2). The matrix A(O) is positive definite in the stated parameter range, and all dimension-half exponents use real division.
For every O, t is absolutely integrable with respect to γ(O), the function x↦t(x)p(O,x) is absolutely integrable with respect to canonical Euclidean volume, and the integral of t under γ(O) equals the volume integral of t(x)p(O,x). Moreover O↦det(O) times the integral of t under γ(O) is absolutely integrable with respect to H, and its Haar integral is exactly
[ (−1)^(n−1)(sqrt(κ)−1)^(n−1) / 2^(n/2) ] times the Haar integral over O(n) of [ ((sqrt(κ)+1)U(O)−(sqrt(κ)−1)) / a(O)^(n/2) ].
All integrability claims and the equality between Gaussian and volume integrals are conclusions, not additional hypotheses; the equality for the Gaussian and volume integrals holds for every O, not merely almost everywhere. The outer measure is normalized Haar measure on the full orthogonal group, and the norm and volume are the true Euclidean ones.
objects: The full real orthogonal group O(n), its normalized Haar probability H, Euclidean Rⁿ with its usual norm and volume, U(O)=O₀₀, a(O)=κ+1+4ℓ−(κ−1)U(O), A(O)=((κ+1)/2)I−((κ−1)/4)(O+Oᵀ), t(x)=exp(−ℓ‖x‖²), p(O,x)=sqrt(det A(O))/(2π)^(n/2) exp(−xᵀA(O)x/2), and the existing centered multivariate Gaussian γ(O) with covariance A(O)⁻¹.
domains: n is a natural number; κ and ℓ are real numbers; O ranges over the full orthogonal group of real n by n matrices with both determinant signs and inherited matrix Borel structure; x ranges over true Euclidean Rⁿ. Inner Gaussian integrals use γ(O), volume integrals use canonical Euclidean volume, and outer integrals use canonical normalized full-group Haar probability H.
quantifiers: For every n with 3≤n, every real κ with 4≤κ, and every real ℓ with 0≤ℓ, define the displayed objects. For every O both inner integrability claims and their integral equality hold. Outer signed integrability and the exact Haar-average identity hold for each such parameter triple.
assumptions: Only n∈N with n≥3, κ∈R with κ≥4, and ℓ∈R with ℓ≥0 are external hypotheses. Orthogonality is supplied by membership in O(n). Positive definiteness of A(O) is justified in this parameter range by the approved context. No integrability or integral-transport identity is assumed.
conclusion: For every O, t belongs to L¹(γ(O)), t(·)p(O,·) belongs to L¹(volume), and ∫t dγ(O)=∫t(x)p(O,x) dx. The function O↦det(O)∫t dγ(O) belongs to L¹(H), and ∫det(O)[∫t dγ(O)] dH(O) equals ((−1)^(n−1)(sqrt(κ)−1)^(n−1)/2^(n/2))∫[((sqrt(κ)+1)U(O)−(sqrt(κ)−1))/a(O)^(n/2)] dH(O).
scopes: Definitions of U, a, p, t, and γ are local to each fixed admissible n, κ, ℓ. The coordinate index 0 is valid because n≥3. The inner claims hold pointwise for every O. The outer signed integral is over full O(n), and det(O) is an explicit sign weight. All L¹ statements are absolute Bochner integrability. Dimension-half exponents use real n/2; n−1 uses natural-number subtraction. The theorem makes no separately stated L¹ claim for the final right-hand-side integrand.
constant_dependencies: There are no existential or unspecified constants. The exact prefactor is (−1)^(n−1)(sqrt(κ)−1)^(n−1)/2^(n/2), depending only on n and κ. The right-hand integrand additionally depends on ℓ through a(O). The test function depends on ℓ; A(O), p(O,·), and γ(O) depend on n, κ, and O. Haar measure depends on n and is normalized to probability; π and the numerical coefficients are universal.
